title: paged-kv-cache: block allocator reuse + pin hot blocks to GPU memory
author: Maya Patel
description:
Context:
The PagedKVCache block manager was frequently allocating and freeing 64KB blocks during steady-state workloads which (1) caused allocator churn and GPU memory fragmentation and (2) increased tail latency for cold prefixes. This PR implements two complementary changes: reuse of recently-freed block allocator slots to reduce repeated allocation overhead, and an optional "pin hot blocks" feature that pins frequently-accessed blocks to GPU resident memory for the life of the inference session.

What this PR does (single continuous description): Adds a reusable block pool to the PagedKVCache BlockManager that keeps recently-released blocks in a size-classed free-list for fast reallocation, implements a lightweight LRU-based hot-block tracker that marks blocks as "pinned" when they exceed a per-session access threshold, exposes a new BlockManagerConfig to tune reuse window and pin thresholds, and updates schedulers to prefer pinned blocks when routing KV fetches. Includes unit tests, integration tests in perf-canary, benchmark harness updates, and operational metrics (allocator_reuse_hits, allocator_reuse_misses, pinned_blocks_count, pinned_block_evictions).

Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked in Linear (ENG-8421) - [x] Unit tests for BlockManager reuse and pin eviction - [x] Integration smoke test in perf-canary - [x] Perf microbenchmark showing reduced p99 and increased throughput - [x] Metrics and dashboards updated

Motivation and impact: Reducing allocator churn reduces CPU/GPU sync overhead and fragmentation. Pinning hot blocks avoids repeated device host transfers for bounded working sets (e.g., few-shot generation with long KV reuse). Microbenchmarks show ~9-12% improvement in p99 token latency and ~6% increase in sustained throughput on our 8xA100 cluster for sample conversational workloads. This is a targeted change that can be toggled per-deployment via BlockManagerConfig, so it is safe to roll out gradually.

Risks and mitigations: Pinning increases GPU-resident memory usage; default config pins only small fraction (<5%) of blocks and we expose a soft eviction policy and metrics to observe memory pressure. Reuse window has sane defaults to avoid long-lived fragmentation.

Notes: This PR touches hot-path code; please review allocator invariants carefully.
